title: How to hide cursor in Finder on Mac: solutions for a cleaner desktop experience
metaTitle: How to hide cursor on Mac: Quickest methods for 2026
description: Learn how to hide cursor on Mac effectively. While macOS lacks a native setting, we cover the best third-party tools for screen recording and presentations.
targetKeyword: how to hide cursor on mac
intro: There is no native, system-wide setting in macOS to hide the mouse cursor in Finder or across the desktop. You must rely on third-party utilities to toggle cursor visibility for presentations or screen recordings.
tldr: macOS does not include a feature to hide the mouse cursor.
Third-party apps like Cursorcerer or Mouse Hider are required.
These tools allow you to hide the cursor via keyboard shortcuts.
Always download utilities from the Mac App Store or reputable developer sites.

blocks.text: Why macOS lacks a hide cursor setting

Apple designs macOS to keep the cursor visible at all times. This is a core accessibility feature. It ensures you always know where your input focus is located. Without a visible cursor, navigating the desktop becomes difficult for many users. The system treats the cursor as a permanent interface element. It does not provide a toggle in System Settings to disable it. Even if you use full keyboard access, the system forces the cursor to appear if you nudge the mouse.
Using third-party tools to hide the cursor

Since you cannot change this in the system, you need a helper app. These apps act as a bridge. They intercept the cursor signal and tell the system to stop rendering it. Popular choices include Cursorcerer, StealthPointer, and Mouse Hider. Each works slightly differently. Some use a global hotkey. Others use an idle timer. You can set them to hide the cursor after a few seconds of inactivity. This is perfect for when you are recording a video or giving a presentation.

Sometimes your hide cursor shortcut will not work. This often happens because another app claims the same key combination. You should check your system settings to see what is using your keys. Open Apple Menu > System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts. Look through the list for any conflicts. If you find one, change the shortcut for the other app. This keeps your system running smoothly while letting you hide the cursor when needed.

blocks.caption: Comparison of common cursor hiding utilities for macOS.

blocks.text: If the cursor pops back up immediately, check your app settings. Many tools have an option called Always show cursor if moved. If this is checked, the slightest vibration of your mouse will reveal the pointer. Disable this setting if you want the cursor to stay hidden until you press your chosen shortcut again. Also, ensure the app has the necessary permissions in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility.

Some games or professional apps override system-level cursor behavior. If an app forces the cursor to be visible, a third-party tool might not be able to hide it. This is not a bug in the utility. It is the app telling the system that a cursor is required for interaction. In these cases, you may need to look for an internal setting within that specific application to hide the mouse pointer.

When you record your screen, a distracting cursor can ruin the flow. Use a consistent hide cursor shortcut. Practice your movements before you start recording. If you are doing a live presentation, keep the cursor hidden until you need to point at something specific. This keeps the audience focused on your content. Remember to turn the cursor back on before you end your session.
Why security matters with these tools

You are giving these apps control over your input. Only download them from trusted sources. The Mac App Store is the safest place to look. If you download from a website, verify the developer. Check the reviews and community discussions. A small utility should not ask for excessive permissions. If it asks for network access or disk permissions, be cautious. Stick to simple, focused tools that do one thing well.

faq.question: Is there a native way to hide the cursor on Mac?
faq.answer: No, macOS does not provide a setting to hide the mouse cursor. It is a system-wide requirement for accessibility.

faq.question: Will these tools work on all macOS versions?
faq.answer: Most utilities are compatible with recent versions, but always check the developer's site for specific macOS 27 compatibility.

faq.question: Why does my cursor keep reappearing?
faq.answer: Check your utility settings for an option like Always show cursor if moved and disable it.

steps.name: Download a utility
steps.text: Download a tool like Cursorcerer from the developer website or Mac App Store.
steps.tip: Only use trusted sources for system utilities.

steps.name: Grant permissions
steps.text: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility and add the app to the list.

steps.name: Configure the shortcut
steps.text: Open the app preferences and set a global hotkey to toggle cursor visibility.

steps.name: Test the hide function
steps.text: Press your shortcut key to hide the cursor and move your mouse to check if it stays hidden.
steps.tip: Ensure the 'Always show if moved' setting is off.

troubleshooting.fix: Check for conflicting shortcuts in System Settings > Keyboard.
Disable the 'Always show cursor if moved' option in your utility.
